description: Hey everyone! I'm a DIPIKA BARMAN ,first-year Btech student putting together a team Hack_The_Stack for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. You don't need to be a coding pro or space expert to join—just bring your curiosity, creativity, and willingness to learn. Let's team up, build something cool together.
summary:
ORBITAL is an interactive, zero-dependency 3D aerospace engineering and space mission simulation game built directly for the web. Traditional space education tools are either static textbook formulas or heavy desktop simulations requiring massive downloads. ORBITAL bridges this gap by combining rigorous orbital mechanics and spacecraft systems engineering with an accessible, cinematic 3D experience.
Players act as space agency directors tasked with planning and executing real-world-inspired planetary campaigns—from lunar water-ice exploration to interplanetary Mars transfers and near-Earth asteroid rendezvous. Using an interactive 3D CAD assembly bay, players must balance authentic aerospace constraints including Delta-v budgets, inverse-square solar irradiance drop-offs, deep-space communication link budgets, thermal/radiation shielding, and launch vehicle payload limits before launching into orbit, surviving mid-flight anomalies, and conducting remote sensing science
details:
1. What does it do / How does it work?

What it does: ORBITAL is a playable, browser-based 3D aerospace mission simulator where you act as a space agency director. You design deep-space spacecraft, select a launch vehicle, survive in-flight space emergencies, and explore destinations like the Moon, Mars, or asteroids.

How it works:

1. Mission Selection: Choose a campaign (Lunar, Mars, or Asteroid) modeled on real NASA planetary data (distances, temperatures, and solar power drop-offs).

2. 3D CAD Assembly: Build your ship piece-by-piece in an interactive 3D workshop, choosing engines, solar panels, antennas, and scientific instruments.

3. Physics Check: The game automatically calculates real rocket math (like fuel weight vs. engine thrust) to verify if your ship can actually make the trip.

4. Launch & Flight: Watch a cinematic 3D launch, navigate through space while handling solar storms, and scan destination planets to earn a NASA letter grade.

2. What benefit does it have?

Interactive Learning: Traditional space education is often locked behind static textbooks or heavy desktop software downloads. ORBITAL makes complex aerospace engineering fun, visual, and accessible to students, teachers, and space enthusiasts anywhere.

Zero-Friction Access: Because it runs directly in any modern web browser without requiring heavy file downloads or external 3D asset servers, anyone can open a link and start learning rocket science immediately.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Inspiring Future Engineers: To spark curiosity in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math) by showing players why real space missions require careful planning, budget management, and problem-solving.

Bridging Theory and Play: To turn abstract math formulas (like rocket equations and solar power laws) into intuitive gameplay where players immediately see the real-world consequences of their engineering choices.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop the project?

Frontend & UI: React 18, Vite 5, Tailwind CSS (for the custom cyber-HUD interface), and Lucide React.

3D Graphics: Three.js (using custom math shaders and procedural canvas textures for planets, stars, and metal foil, avoiding heavy external image downloads).

Audio Engine: Web Audio API (to generate real-time countdown beeps, rocket engine rumbles, and telemetry sounds through code).

Data Persistence: Browser LocalStorage to save mission progress automatically.

NASA Reference Data:

NASA Planetary Fact Sheets (NSSDCA) for planetary distances, gravity, and solar irradiance values.

NASA TechPort & Small Spacecraft Tech Reports for hardware subsystem specifications (ion thrusters, solar arrays, shielding).

5. How is your project creative?

100% Procedural 3D Assets: Instead of slowing down the browser by loading massive 3D model files and texture images, everything from the planetary surfaces to the thermal foil wrapping on the spacecraft is generated procedurally using math and code.

Real Physics as Gameplay Mechanics: Rather than treating math as a boring quiz, the game turns authentic aerospace constraints (like balancing solar power drop-offs at Mars or managing fuel weight) into engaging puzzle mechanics.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Browser Performance & Speed: We designed the app to be lightweight, fast-loading, and easily deployable on cloud platforms like Vercel without relying on external media servers.

Scientific Accuracy vs. Playability: We carefully balanced authentic NASA physics (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, inverse-square solar law) with smooth, intuitive gameplay so players learn real science without feeling overwhelmed.
dataRefs: Used to benchmark real-world subsystem trade-offs (specific impulse, power draw, mass, and link-budget gain) for our modular spacecraft components, including ion thrusters, GaAs solar arrays, high-gain dishes, MLI shielding, and scientific instruments.
Used for planetary orbital distances, surface gravity, solar irradiance (1/d^2), and environmental parameters for the Lunar, Mars, and Asteroid mission dossiers.
